source.name: OpenDota
source.queryParameters: none -- no patch, rank or time-window parameter is sent

rulesetTarget.meaning: product target; NOT a claim about what the data measured

patchClaim.label: 7.41e
patchClaim.basis: caller-supplied constant stamped at ingestion (CURRENT_PATCH); the source reports no patch
patchClaim.appliesTo: hero_patch_stats.patch only; hero_matchups has no patch column

observationWindowNote: not reported by OpenDota and not recorded by the sync; unknown, NOT assumed equal to any patch

sample.heroStatsBracketDefinition: OpenDota /heroStats `<tier>_pick`/`<tier>_win`, tier 1..8 labelled herald..immortal by the project; the MMR span of each tier is not recorded here
sample.matchupSampleDefinition: per (hero, opposing hero) aggregate games/wins from /heroes/{id}/matchups; no bracket split, window unknown

hashes.logicalFingerprintScope: heroes(id,localized_name,roles) + hero_patch_stats(hero_id,patch,bracket,picks,wins) + hero_matchups(hero_id,vs_hero_id,games,wins); independent of file layout and meta_sync

limitations: The patch label is applied by our ingestion, not reported by OpenDota: it is UNVERIFIED and must not be read as "data is from that patch".
The ruleset target (7.41f) and the data label (7.41e) are different things; equality or inequality between them proves nothing about the data.
The observation window OpenDota aggregated over is unknown: nothing here dates the games themselves.
hero_matchups carries no patch and no bracket: it can never be attributed to a patch, even in principle.

A sync run is recorded as not finished: the frozen rows are the union of what was committed before it stopped and earlier complete runs (each hero's matchups are written in one transaction, so a hero's block is internally consistent, but blocks were retrieved at different times).
hero_matchups was retrieved in 2 separate groups (see synchronization.matchupRetrievalGroups).
Bracket(s) with zero recorded picks for every hero: immortal.
